label: conj:complex-mass-constituent-functional
title: Complex-mass constituent functional
html:
Conjecture (complex-mass constituent functional). There is a single complex-mass functional \mathfrak{M} on the composite braid / Hecke-module state space whose real part, projected onto per-generation flavour blocks, reproduces the light quark doublet and determines the heavy-flavour masses with no per-flavour tuning.

The quark masses are not hyperbolic volumes of independent per-quark knots: the Standard-Model appendix records that no carrier knot exists for \mathfrak{s}, \mathfrak{c}, \mathfrak{b}, \mathfrak{t}. Each quark is instead a constituent of a composite braid, and its mass is a functional of that composite. We generalise the real volume reading m(K) = m_e\,\mathrm{Vol}(K)\,\varrho(K)/\hbar_q^2 in two ways.

  1. Real volume \to complex volume. \mathrm{Vol}(K) \rightsquigarrow \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathbb{C}}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K) + i\,\mathrm{CS}(K), the Chern–Simons invariant supplying the imaginary partner already used for \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}. The physical mass is the real part; the imaginary part is the confinement / instability scale — the Breit–Wigner width of a confined constituent that never has a real pole mass.

  2. Per-knot scalar \to spectrum of a functional. \mathfrak{M} acts on the composite's Hecke module; the six quark masses are the real parts of its Frobenius-block projections \mathfrak{M}|_\lambda, the block \lambda carrying the generation winding n (with n = 3, 5, 7 the torus-knot longitudinal windings of the three generations).

No-tuning content. Successive generations are tied by the fixed continuant ratio b_n / b_{n-2} of the Morgan–Voyce tower — the same tower whose divisibility b_a \mid b_n \Leftrightarrow a \mid n fixes which windings are generations. So the second-generation (charm) block is determined by the first-generation block, with no free per-flavour parameter; the light-doublet splitting \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}, which the substrate already fixes, is the single calibrated anchor.

Falsifiability. Both the Chern–Simons invariant and the composite braid are rigid — zero free parameters once the hadron's quark content fixes the braid — so the conjecture predicts the strange / charm splitting with nothing left to tune. The Lean class QOU.MassTheory.ComplexMassConstituent carries this as two content fields, the winding-tower law and the light-doublet anchor, and the sorry-free conditional theorem charm_block_determined shows the charm block equals \mathrm{contRatio}(5) times the up block.

Status: OPEN (primary conjecture). No instance of the class is exhibited. Constructing the categorically-fixed functional \mathfrak{M} — equivalently deriving \mathrm{contRatio} and the block projections from the Frobenius pairing \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda — is the open closure, and until it is done no second-generation quark mass follows. This is a formalize-first scaffold, not a derivation: it states a falsifiable claim and its consequence structure. It sits in Subgoal-2 research (open for all agents); the anti-fit discipline gates how it may be closed — a \mathfrak{M} obtained by inverting the quark-mass anchors is a fit, not a derivation, and may not be wired to production as canonical.
